This game saved my life.

I am 35.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.

After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.

Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.

After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.

Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.

I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.

Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

Definitely an interesting concept for a game. I had issues with the opening sequence playing properly, but other than that, the game ran pretty smoothly (which is a feat on my computer). I enjoyed being able to explore the idea of what a national surveillance system would potentially look like, how reliant it would be on something as malleable as human opinion and how vulnerable it would be to error or abuse. Instead of playing the game as someone living under the system, you are a part of the system. You are the one spying on these people and handing over their personal and/or private information to the government. You choose what information to include or exclude. Whether these people live free, die, or spend life in prison is entirely dependent on what information YOU give to your superiors. And your opinion can be swayed. The choices you make may have fatal consequences.
Overall, an enjoyable game, played in a couple sittings. One of only a few games I wanted to get all the achievements in and felt it was actually achievable.

Although I got stuck a couple of times for 5-10 minutes just clicking around pages until I found something I'd missed, generally the game does a good job of holding your hand enough that you don't get lost in the amount of information available to you without making it so obvious that its just pointing and clicking. I did get a little confused by the big ending and exactly what I was supposed to do to finish on the ending I wanted - I feel like a pop up to click an option might have been a little easier. All in all a very good game and a fun 3-4 hours if you've got the time spare!

I didn’t know what to expect going into Orwell, but was delighted by its engaging storytelling and effective worldbuilding. In this game, you play as an employee of a fictional government tasked with investigating a terrorist attack. To this end, you utilise the “Orwell” system to monitor the online activity, history, and live chats of persons of interest. This plays like a hybrid of visual novels and point-and-click adventure games, as you scroll in-game websites and remote desktops to find information relevant to the case.

The game’s real achievement is that despite its ambitious concept, Orwell offers a great balance of freedom and guidance. There is just enough secondary or irrelevant information available to you that discovering a new clue feels groundbreaking and rewarding. At the same time, pages containing unread details are marked on your menu and guiding commentary from your handler keeps the game moving at a decent pace. I never felt lost or stuck about what to read or add to a suspect’s profile, apart from the intended moments of contradiction or misinterpretation which I won’t spoil here.

I highly recommend this to people who enjoy detective games like “Her Story” or even sci-fi noir like “Deus Ex”. I’ll definitely play this again to try for another ending!

Orwell is a fantastic commentary on state surveillance. The story, whilst only about five hours long, perfectly captures the dangers of mass surveillance and of the unfair consequences it can have on the daily lives of innocent people. This game shows you first-hand what arguments can be made for the notion of a 'Police State,' and by the end of the story, how these arguments are false dichotomies at best; used by people in power to justify total control over a population. I think this game holds itself up very well, even compared to the masterpiece that is Papers Please, and is absolutely a worthwhile experience.

Clearly one of the most controversial and contemporary games you'll ever find, Orwell surely in one finest example of a masterpiece.
First and foremost, although this game is set in a fictional nation, ( called The Nation, which I believe is quite intentional to max the immersivity factor) this game keeps things ''real'', in  a most disturbing matter, I might add.
Gameplay and story wise, you'll spy on some citizens of this nation connected to a terrorist act.
You'll do so by going through articles, reports, their electronic devices, ect.. like in a real investigation.
But, as you can clearly imagine, the gameplay and story is just there to highlight the idea behind the game:  how easily privacy can be broken with the right tools and how easily one can use the fear for safety to limit freedom to a nation ( I mean, it's right there on the Title, so it's not like the developers intentions were so obscure).
The astonishing fact is how the game manages to convey this idea: fluidly and graciously creepy.
As one interested in such topics and as a reader of Orwell's novels myself ( Which, I believe, all should read at least one in their lifetime ) it is refreshing to see a game about media manipulation and secret police done quite right ( I was gonna add ''cyberpunk'' to the list of things that this game is... but since we have reached a certain point in technological evolution, it's  safe to say that is really a frightening and possible reality).
Also, the game never guides too much the player and never gives multiple solutions to a particular problem.
So, Is it worth buying? Yes, absolutely. Actually, I would say it should be MANDATORY ( the irony isn't lost on me) for gamers of any age to play this game.
And if don't agree... just remember, big brother is always watching 0-0

This review doesn't contain spoilers:

This is a brilliant game! I've never played anything like it before and now I'm interested in buying the next season in the series.

Simple Plot: Basically you play an intelligence agent tasked to investigate the events around a terror attack in a fictional country that's run by an Orwellian government. 

Gameplay: Text based but accompanied by rather interesting visuals and calm music. Your character (basically you) can monitor citizens computers, phones, bank accounts etc secretly, while building profiles for them and submitting data you think is incriminating up to your bosses. There's a lot of skimming through data, but it's worth it because you start unravelling a storyline and secrets people hide from each other. You're basically playing something like a simulated intelligence agent screen. There are 5 days which will take about 6-ish hours to complete the game if you play nonstop.

Graphics: Smooth and nice but it doesn't really take up much to generate the graphics in this game as much of the game is texts and chat boxes. The art style of people are picasso-ish and there's only one animated scene at the beginning of the game.

Value: I've never played any kind of text based game before so this opened up a whole new world of experience for me! I really enjoyed it so I felt it was worth it! The other thing is that there are multiple endings you could choose so you can replay the game several times to choose different endings. Achievement hunting is rather easy and doesn't require much skill but rather to make different choices in the game.

7/10

How do you keep privacy in the age of information?
Orwell is a game about freedom of thoughts, in a world where that very same freedom gives way to danger. What could the criminals be hiding in those text convos and phone calls? That's for you to find out. Are they planning to strike x or y? That's for you to find out. Are they criminals in the first place, or are they just tokens in someone else's game?
Orwell makes you constantly think and question about how you judge people, who naturally keep secrets and lie in everyday life. How can you know a person, and yet know nothing at all at the same time? How do you know this line of data risks that same person's life?
It's a constant battle of what are you willing to upload, and what to keep hidden. First time in forever has a single line of uploaded text changed the course of the game so radically to the point where I didn't want to go on. What a brilliant consept, and what a brilliant execution. [i]Die Gedanken sind frei - Thoughts are free.[/i]

[h1] Interactive story hidden behind a simple detective game [/h1]

While the game's premise sounds pretty interesting, the gameplay is quite simple. You read various things such as Internet pages (forums, bank account extract, company's webpage, etc), chat discussions,  listen to live calls which are transcribed and some parts of the text will be highlighted which you can then drag and drop to [b]Orwell[/b], a database which unlocks additional things if a link can be established with the information you've taken.
For a non-spoiler example: you search a person's personal blog and you can find and analyze their username which can then be linked to another forum where it's used for more juicy contents.

It's a bit like [u]A Lost Phone[/u] but its puzzles are MUCH simpler and you can't really get stuck for too long as there's plenty of helpful indicators. Actually, the best part of the game where I really concentrated was when the amount of datachunks (highlighted parts of data in texts) you could import was limited. This really made you think if a [strike]favorite color[/strike] hobby such as artist is a valuable piece of data or not (you could be redirected to an artist page showing past gigs/locations or a contact phone number!).

The best part of the game is the story, because in the end, there's a story and it's told little by little, there are some interesting plot parts (Sorry won't spoil anything) and even if the gameplay sounds boring, the pace is really good and I didn't see time pass by while I finished the 5 episodes. It takes a little bit more than one hour per episode, maybe faster if you just drag and drop without reading.
Even if having a [i]know it all[/i] tool, there are plenty of mysteries to uncover and discovering bit by bit the personalities and relationships of the people you [strike]spy on[/strike] is pretty addictive.

The presentation is pretty nice with its stylish interface. Graphics isn't the most important part of the game but it's good that it's pleasing to the eyes. The music does also its job, it changes when there's a [b]gasp[/b] moment. 

In summary, I recommend this game if you like simple but well told story in a different way than just watching Netflix. It has a nice conspiracy/detective vibe and getting to the finish is an entertaining (and bumpy) ride.
